Use the model above to solve the following multiplication problem. You do not need to simplify your answer.

$\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{2}{3}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to multiply by $\frac{2}{3}$, we split the whole into $3$ equal parts horizontally and ensure that $2$ of the parts remain shaded.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14130839/assets/815da3d43a92c55492a14fc8fd20a5dfdcacd881db9442f9b302b202d55554e9.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\frac{2}{6}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{2}{3}=\frac{2}{6}.
$$
